_readme: informationClass implements DEC-003 section 1 and is required on every entry. Allowed values: architecture_rule, project_context, personal_reference.

An entry with a missing or unknown informationClass is not dropped - it falls back to project_context, the most restrictive class. A misconfiguration therefore makes an answer more careful, never more authoritative.

reviewedAt is the date the document was last deliberately checked against reality (DEC-003 section 3, status 'geprueft'). It is maintained for project_context and personal_reference; architecture_rule needs none, because an Accepted DEC's validity follows from its own version and status, not from a review date.
reviewedAt may be null when the document carries no review date at all. It is then rendered as 'nicht datiert' rather than being invented.

KNOWN LIMIT (accepted for P1-A3): reviewedAt is maintained here, not derived from the document. Editing a vault note without updating this date makes the date misleading. The content fingerprint (P1-A2) still detects the edit; the date does not.

These fields are NOT part of the allowlist fingerprint (see canonicalAllowlistIdentity in orchestrator/knowledge/rag-fingerprint.js, which hashes relativePath only). Changing them takes effect on the next request without invalidating the index and without requiring a re-index - correct, because they do not influence any embedding.
